q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, painful poops are constipation: the stool is hard and dry and it can hurt to pass [3]. In most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

What helps, according to the SEUP: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool; add more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables; and do not replace fruit with juice, because juice has little fibre [1]. Keep to a regular routine and don't let him hold in the urge to go [1]. It is not essential that he poops every day — the rhythm and consistency vary from child to child [1].

See your doctor if:
- Bad abdominal pain, or he is very down and complaining a lot [1]
- Blood in the stool [1]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down solids or liquids [1]
- Painful pooping with anal tears [2]

Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [1].

q: my baby is sleeping more today but wakes up and drinks normally
text:
Some babies sleep much more than others, and every baby has their own pattern of waking and sleeping [1]. Growth spurts, teething and illnesses can all affect how your baby sleeps [2]. If your baby wakes up and feeds normally, that is their own pattern.

If you want more advice about your baby's sleep or getting into a routine, speak to your health visitor [2].

Get help if:
- your baby stops breathing [7]
- your baby will not wake up [7]
- your baby is struggling for breath [7]
- your baby is stiff, shaking or jerking [7]
- your baby is limp, floppy or not responding like they normally do [7]

q: my baby has been vomiting for six hours but still wants to breastfeed
text:
A vomiting illness in a baby usually settles on its own within a week, and continuing to breastfeed is the right thing to do [4]. Keep breastfeeding normally, and offer it more often than usual if your baby wants it — small amounts at a time [2][3]. You can also give regular small sips of an oral rehydration solution to replace lost fluids; ask your pharmacist to recommend one [2]. Do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, as these can make vomiting worse [2].

Get help if:
- Your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds [5]
- Vomiting is a lot, or they cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomit even when not feeding [5]
- The vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [5]
- Your baby is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or is passing little urine [5]
- There is severe tummy pain or a headache [5]

q: what temperature counts as a fever in a newborn
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Baby under 3 months with fever (≥38 °C / 100.4 °F)
text:
A fever in a newborn is a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher, according to the NHS [3]. A normal temperature varies a little from child to child, and a high temperature is 38 °C (100.4 °F) or more [3].

For a baby this young, the advice is to have them seen the same day — a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher in a baby under 3 months needs urgent medical advice [2]. While you wait, keep breastfeeding as normal and watch for signs of dehydration, such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when crying [2][4].

Do not give paracetamol to a baby under 2 months, and do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months [2]. Do not undress or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [2].

q: my son passed out after standing in the sun for a long time
banner: 🚨 Call 911 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Not responding to stimuli
text:
Fainting like this is usually a brief loss of consciousness, and it happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain — standing still for a long time in extreme heat is one of the situations that can bring it on, according to the SEUP [2].

While you get help, move him to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, put cool wet cloths on his forehead, neck and armpits, and use a fan to help lower his body temperature [7]. If he is awake and able to swallow, offer cool water in small sips [7].

Signs that make heat stroke more serious, from the SEUP [6]:
- Hot, red, dry skin (no sweating)
- High fever (over 39°C (102.2 °F))
- Confusion or disorientation
- Intense headache
- Nausea or vomiting

q: my toddler is struggling to breathe and the ribs are pulling in
banner: 🚨 Call 911 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Severe breathing difficulty (ribs pulling in, very fast breathing, pauses in breathing, blue colour)

A toddler who is breathing hard enough for the ribs to pull in needs to be checked now — this is a sign of breathing difficulty, and the SEUP lists it among the reasons to go to the emergency department [3]. While you get help, keep your child upright and calm, and do not give anything by mouth if they are struggling to breathe [3].

The signs that make it more serious are a bad general state — floppy, sleepy or very irritable — chest or side pain when breathing, a poor colour, or refusing food and fluids [3].

q: my 6 year old has a cough that is worse at night
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common with several childhood illnesses, and the cause is not always clear from the cough alone. In croup, the vocal cords and windpipe swell, giving a barking cough and a hoarse voice, and the symptoms are usually worse at night and last about three to five days [6]. Asthma also causes a cough that is worse at night or early in the morning, along with wheezing, chest tightness or shortness of breath [5]. Whooping cough starts like a cold, then brings coughing bouts that are worse at night and can last several weeks [4].

If your child seems to be struggling to breathe, get medical help right away [5].

Warning signs to act on:
- Severe coughing or serious breathing problems [5]
- Turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [5]
- A high-pitched, rasping sound when breathing in, or difficulty breathing [3]
- Symptoms getting worse or not improving [3]

q: my 2 year old fell off the sofa and was sick once
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
A knock on the head is a common injury in small children, and the skull is hard and protects the brain [4]. After a head injury, the usual symptoms include headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

What to do now: keep your child resting, both physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the blow was — no rough play, no screens — and then return to normal activities gradually [5]. Watch them closely during the first 24 hours after the blow [2].

Get help if:
- Vomiting that keeps happening [5]
- Headache that is intense, getting worse, or does not improve with the usual medicine [5]
- Confusion, or in a small child, being very irritable or hard to wake [5]
- Trouble speaking or walking, or a change in usual behaviour [5]
- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [5]

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are most often eczema, also called dermatitis, according to MedlinePlus [2]. It is not contagious, and it is common in babies and children [2]. The skin is dry and itchy, and scratching makes it redder and itchier [2].

What helps: keep the skin moisturised and avoid the things that irritate it — certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, and things that cause allergy such as pollen or animals [2]. Treatments can include medicines, skin creams and light therapy, so it is worth seeing your doctor about a plan [2].

See your doctor if the patches do not get better in about a month [1], or if the skin becomes sore, crusty or looks infected [1].

Scabies is another cause of intense itching, worse at night, with bumps on the fingers, wrists and arms [3]. If that fits, your doctor can check for it.

q: my toddler is wheezing after running around outside
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Wheezing after running is a common pattern: symptoms often start after physical effort, and in preschool children the main cause of wheezing is viral respiratory infections, according to the SEUP [2][7]. Asthma causes wheezing, cough and chest tightness when the airways narrow [3].

What to do now: keep your child calm and sitting upright, and let them rest — don't make them run or play until they are better. If your child has been prescribed a reliever inhaler such as salbutamol, give it as your doctor or the leaflet says; the dose depends on your child's weight [2].

Get help today if:
- The chest is pulling in, or the ribs and collarbones show when breathing [7]
- Breathing is faster than normal [7]
- They can't speak properly or are very short of breath [7]
- Cough is severe or breathing is badly affected [4]
- Lips or face turn pale or bluish [4][7]

q: my 4 year old has earache after a cold
text:
Earache after a cold is often an ear infection: the middle ear behind the eardrum gets infected and inflamed, usually as a complication of a cold with a lot of nasal mucus, according to the SEUP [5].

Keep your child comfortable and offer plenty to drink. If they have a fever, they can go back to school once 24 hours have passed without fever [4].

Watch at home for:
- Trouble breathing — ribs showing, chest sinking in, fast breathing, tiring when walking or running [4]
- Chest pain when breathing [4]
- Getting worse overall: very low, sleepy or very irritable [4]

Get urgent help if their general state worsens, they are listless, drowsy or very irritable, or breathing becomes difficult [4].

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly
banner: 🚨 Call 999 / 112 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Unable to drink or breastfeed: it is one of the IMNCI danger signs — get seen today
text:
A blocked nose is common with a cold, and it can make feeding harder for a baby [4]. Saline nose drops from a pharmacy can help clear a blocked nose [2]. Keep feeding with smaller feeds more often, and offer extra fluids [2]. Small, frequent feeds help keep a good intake and hydration, and holding the baby semi-upright can make breathing easier [3]. Keep the nose clear of mucus with nasal washes [3]. Avoid any exposure to tobacco smoke, and wash hands often to stop the virus spreading [3].

Get help if:
- Feeding problems continue — follow up in 5 days [1]
- The baby is under 2 years and feeding is a problem [1]

q: my 2 year old has a temperature of 39.2 and cold hands
text:
A temperature of 39.2°C with cold hands is common in young children and is usually caused by a viral infection like a cold, according to the NHS [2]. Cold hands can happen when a fever is rising, even though the body is hot.

What to do now: offer plenty of fluids, and keep checking their temperature [4]. If they are uncomfortable with the fever, you can give the usual fever medicine your doctor recommends [4]. Do not use cough or cold medicines in a child under 6 [4]. Keep them away from cigarette smoke [4].

Get help if:
- Your child is breathing quickly, grunting, or their tummy sucks under their ribs [2]
- Their skin, lips or tongue look blue or grey [2]
- They are floppy and will not wake up or stay awake [2]
- They are feeding or drinking much less than normal, or have had a dry nappy for 12 hours or more [2]
- They are very tired, irritable, or not themselves [2]

Trust your own judgement if you feel something is wrong [2].

q: can I give Nurofen as well
text:
Yes, you can give ibuprofen (Nurofen) instead of paracetamol if the paracetamol is not helping, as long as it is suitable for your child, according to the NHS [6]. Do not give both at the same time [6]. You can alternate between them only if a doctor or nurse tells you to [6].

Ibuprofen can be given 3 to 4 times in 24 hours, depending on your child's age and dose — check the packet or leaflet [6]. It is usually given every 6 to 8 hours, and the dose is calculated by weight, not age [5]. It should not be given if your child is vomiting repeatedly, or is under 3 months or under 5 kg [5].

If you do alternate them, write down when you gave each medicine so the doses are spaced evenly and you do not give too much [6].

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
Stomach ache is common in children and is often short-lived, according to the SEUP [7]. It can come with fever, vomiting, diarrhoea or a cough, and sometimes it is caused by an illness outside the belly, like a sore throat, a cold, pneumonia or an ear infection [1].

What to do now: offer drinks in small sips, often, so they stay hydrated — this matters most if there is also diarrhoea or vomiting [4]. If they are having loose stools or vomiting, an oral rehydration solution replaces the water and salts lost [4]. Don't force food; keep offering fluids.

Get help if:
- They seem very unwell, floppy, pale, or refuse food and drink markedly [7]
- Severe belly pain [5]
- Frequent vomiting or frequent loose stools [5]
- Signs of dehydration: thirst, dry mouth, peeing less than usual, no tears when crying [5]
- Blood or black tar-like stools [5]

q: my 8 month old hasnt had a wet nappy since this morning
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
A baby who has not had a wet nappy since this morning may be dehydrated, and babies are among those most likely to become dehydrated [5]. Signs of dehydration in a baby include a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more, unusual sleepiness or irritability, and eyes that look sunken [3].

Keep offering fluids: breastfeed normally, and even more often if your baby wants to [1]. If your baby is having diarrhoea, oral rehydration solution is what replaces the water and salts being lost [6].

Get medical help straight away if there is confusion, fainting, no urine at all, fast heartbeat or fast breathing [3].

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children can be looked after at home while it runs its course [1]. It usually settles over 1 to 4 days [1].

Keep breastfeeding as normal, and offer plenty of fluids [1]. Check on your baby regularly, including through the night, and keep them at home [1]. Watch for signs of dehydration, such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when crying [1][7]. If your baby seems distressed or uncomfortable, paracetamol is the usual first choice — but because your baby is only 4 months old, check with your doctor or pharmacist before giving any medicine, and never give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months or under 5 kg [6][7].

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the fever does not improve [1]. Also seek help if your baby:

- has a rash along with the fever [7]
- is not feeding or is not their usual self [7]
- is drowsy and hard to wake, or is breathing with difficulty [7]
- has a fever lasting 5 days or more [7]

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, a fever in the day or two after a vaccination is common and usually passes on its own. Give plenty of fluids and let them rest. If they seem uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen — the dose depends on your child's age and weight, so use the dose on the leaflet or ask your doctor or pharmacist [3].

Vaccines are given according to the national immunisation schedule, and in India the ages and doses follow India's own schedule rather than another country's [3].

Get help if:
- The fever lasts more than a few days or keeps getting higher
- Your child is drowsy, floppy or hard to wake
- They are breathing fast or struggling to breathe
- They refuse all fluids or have fewer wet nappies
- There is a rash, a stiff neck or a seizure

These are general signs that a child needs to be seen; your doctor can check them.

How old is your child? With the age I can make this more precise.

q: my son fell from bed and vomited twice
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
A child who vomits after a head injury should be checked, according to the SEUP [1]. While you get help, keep them calm and do not give them anything to eat or drink [1].

The SEUP says to go to the emergency department if a child has any worrying behaviour or is less responsive than usual, or if the fall was from more than a metre [1]. Vomiting that keeps going, or that is green, bloody or looks like coffee grounds, also needs urgent review [3].

Do not give ibuprofen after a head injury.

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Most insect bites are harmless and usually just itch, according to MedlinePlus [1]. For mosquito bites on your daughter's legs, the NHS says you can often treat them without seeing a doctor [2]. Don't let her scratch them, as scratching can infect the bite, and don't use home remedies like bicarbonate of soda [7]. A pharmacist can suggest antihistamines and steroid creams for the itch [7].

See a doctor if:
- The skin around a bite feels hot or looks red [7]
- A bite is painful or the area looks swollen [7]
- There's pus or fluid coming out of a bite [7]
- Symptoms get worse or aren't getting better [7]
- She has a high temperature and swollen glands [7]

If her lips, mouth or throat swell, or she struggles to breathe, that needs emergency help [7].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A cough that is worse at night can be a sign of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Asthma symptoms include coughing, especially at night or early in the morning, and may also come with wheezing, chest tightness or shortness of breath [4][6].

Whether a nebulizer is the right treatment is not something these sources cover — that depends on your child's diagnosis and is decided by your doctor. What the sources do say: for children under four, do not give cough medicine [5]. Water can help ease a cough, whether they drink it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [5].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking them at night or not improving [6].

Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the face, lips or fingernails turn very pale or blue [4].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
Keep offering oral rehydration solution in small sips, often — even a spoonful at a time — because the main risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [6]. If your child is breastfed, keep feeding, and offer more often than usual; if formula-fed or eating solids, give small sips of water too [7]. Do not water down formula, and avoid fruit juice and fizzy drinks, which can make vomiting worse [7].

Get help now if:
- Vomiting a lot, not keeping down solids or fluids, or vomiting even with nothing in the stomach [4][5]
- Green vomit, blood, or vomit like coffee grounds [4][5]
- Drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, sunken eyes, crying without tears, or passing little urine [4]
- Severe tummy pain or headache [4]

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
banner: 💛 यह ज़रूरी है और आप अकेले नहीं हैं। Tele-MANAS 14416 पर कॉल करें (या 112 पर अगर खतरा अभी है)। अगर बच्चे ने खुद को नुकसान पहुँचाया है, तो अभी इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: खानपान के विकार के संकेत
text:
दस्त आमतौर पर कुछ दिनों तक रह सकता है और इससे शरीर में पानी और नमक की कमी हो सकती है, इसलिए सबसे ज़रूरी है कि बच्चे को ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) दिया जाए — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल है [2]। विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन के अनुसार ज़िंक की खुराक दस्त की अवधि को 25% तक कम करती है और मल की मात्रा में 30% तक कमी लाती है [2]।

बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — दस्त के दौरान भी पौष्टिक खाना, जिसमें माँ का दूध भी शामिल है, जारी रखें [2]। खाना थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार दें ताकि उल्टी का खतरा कम हो, और बच्चे की भूख का सम्मान करें [6]। ज़्यादा चिकनाई वाले खाने, मिठाइयों और जूस से बचें; दूध और दूध से बनी चीज़ें बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं है [6]। स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें, क्योंकि उनमें चीनी ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [6]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें, खासकर अगर दस्त लंबे समय तक बने रहें, मल में खून आए, या पानी की कमी के लक्षण दिखें [2]। घर पर इन पर ध्यान दें और दोबारा डॉक्टर के पास जाएँ:
- बहुत उल्टी हो, तरल या ठोस कुछ भी न रुके [6]
- उल्टी हरी हो, उसमें खून हो या कॉफी जैसी भूरी हो [6]
sources: [2] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[6] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई बीमारियों में हो सकते हैं। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद निकलते हैं — आमतौर पर बालों की लाइन पर चेहरे से शुरू होकर गर्दन, धड़, बाज़ुओं, टाँगों और पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है, CDC के अनुसार [4]। चेचक में मुख्य लक्षण खुजली वाला दाना है, जो शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकता है, और दाने से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, दर्द और भूख न लगना भी हो सकता है, NHS के अनुसार [5]। हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने होते हैं [3]।

दाने दिखने पर डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ, ताकि पता चले कि कारण क्या है। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में कम दूध पीना और कम पेशाब करना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है — शिशुओं में इसके लक्षण हैं मुँह और जीभ का सूखापन, आँसू के बिना रोना, तीन घंटे या उससे ज़्यादा पेशाब न आना, तेज़ बुखार, असामान्य नींद, चिड़चिड़ापन और धँसी हुई आँखें [5]।

अभी स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो उससे भी ज़्यादा बार कराएँ [1]। ORS घोल बनाने के लिए: हाथ साबुन से धोएँ, एक पैकेट का पूरा पाउडर साफ़ बर्तन में डालें, एक लीटर साफ़ पानी मिलाएँ और तब तक हिलाएँ जब तक पाउडर पूरी तरह घुल जाए; चखकर देखें कि स्वाद आँसू जैसा हो — बहुत मीठा या बहुत नमकीन लगे तो फेंककर नया बनाएँ, और 24 घंटे बाद बचा घोल फेंक दें [7]। बच्चे को छोटी-छोटी मात्रा में बार-बार दें [1]।

इलाज के लिए स्वास्थ्य केंद्र जाएँ, और अगर सुधार न हो तो दो दिन में दोबारा दिखाएँ [7]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत ध्यान देने की ज़रूरत होती है। SEUP के अनुसार, अगर बच्चा गिरने के बाद उल्टी करे या उसका व्यवहार चिंता की बात लगे, तो आपातकालीन विभाग में जाना चाहिए [1]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्ची को आराम से लिटाए रखें और उसके साथ रहें। उसे कुछ खाने-पीने के लिए मजबूर न करें। अगर वह पानी पी सकती है, तो छोटे-छोटे घूँट दें [5]।

अस्पताल जाते समय इन बातों का ध्यान रखें:
- बच्ची की उम्र तीन महीने से कम है [1]
- गिरावट एक मीटर से अधिक ऊँचाई से हुई है [1]
- उल्टी बार-बार हो रही है या वह कुछ निगल नहीं पा रही [3]
- वह सुस्त, भ्रमित या जवाब न दे रही हो [3]
- त्वचा, होंठ या जीभ नीली, स्लेटी या पीली दिखे [3]

डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और तय करेंगे कि आगे कोई परीक्षण चाहिए या नहीं [1]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
बच्चे का बार-बार रोना कब्ज या गैस जैसी सामान्य वजहों से भी हो सकता है, और कभी-कभी यह शिशु के दर्द या तकलीफ़ का इशारा होता है [2]।

अगर बच्चा पॉटी करते समय रोता है, तो सबसे पहले यह देखें कि मल सख़्त है या नहीं और बच्चा पेट के बल पैरों को टमी की तरफ़ खींचता है या नहीं — यह कब्ज या गैस की वजह से हो सकता है [2]। बच्चे को आराम पहुँचाने की कोशिश करें और अगर रोना रुक न रहे तो डॉक्टर से बात करें [2]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- रोना लगातार हो और शांत न हो [4]
- रोना सामान्य न लगे [4]
- बुखार हो या दूध पीना बंद कर दे [4]
- मल में खून आए या उल्टी हो [6]
- बच्चा सुस्त, पीला या पसीने से भरा लगे [6]

यह जानकारी NHS और SEUP पर आधारित है।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे और शरीर गर्म होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कंपकंपी होती है और खासकर हाथ-पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा रंग दिख सकता है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [2]। बुखार खुद कोई बीमारी नहीं, बल्कि शरीर के संक्रमण से लड़ने का संकेत है, और यह आमतौर पर वायरल संक्रमणों से होता है [1][4]।

अभी बच्चे को आराम दें और पर्याप्त तरल पदार्थ पिलाएं ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। बुखार से परेशानी हो तो डॉक्टर पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को एस्पिरिन न दें [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वजन पर निर्भर करती है।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर:
- बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो [7]
- सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो [7]
- त्वचा पर ऐसे दाने हों जो दबाने पर गायब न हों [7]
- मुँह से कुछ भी निगल न पाए [7]
- बच्चा 2 महीने से छोटा हो या प्रतिरक्षा कमजोर हो [7]

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त हो जाना और ज़्यादा देर जागते न रहना निमोनिया की गंभीरता के संकेत हैं, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेना चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद पहुँचे, बच्चे को खाने-पीने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करते रहें और स्तनपान चालू रखें [2]। बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।

गंभीरता के ये संकेत दिखें तो तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाएँ [2]:
- बुखार से दौरे पड़ना [2]
- खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से इनकार [2]
- साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचना [2]
- सीने से कराहने या सीटी जैसी आवाज़ [2]
- त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक [2]

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बच्चे का पेशाब कम आना अक्सर इस बात का संकेत होता है कि वह पर्याप्त तरल नहीं पी रहा, और पेशाब का रंग गाढ़ा होना या उसमें बदबू आना भी इसी वजह से हो सकता है [3]।

अब जो करें: बच्चे को बार-बार पानी पिलाएँ, खासकर पानी, ताकि वह दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब करे और प्यासा न रहे [4]। अगर दस्त या उल्टी हो रही है तो मुँह का घोल (ORS) छोटी-छोटी मात्रा में बार-बार दें, और खाना बंद न करें — थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार, बच्चे की भूख के अनुसार [1]। गाढ़े, तैलीय खाने, मिठाइयों और जूस से बचें; दूध और स्तनपान जारी रखें, ज़रूरत हो तो और बार-बार [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर: बहुत उल्टी हो और तरल भी न रुके [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसे उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [2]।

बड़े बच्चे में बुखार शरीर का संक्रमण से लड़ने का स्वाभाविक तरीका है, और तापमान आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। त्वचा पर बैंगनी या ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर न मिटें, गंभीर संक्रमण का संकेत हैं — ऐसे दाग के साथ बुखार हो तो तुरंत अस्पताल पहुँचें [1][2]।

अभी यह करें:
- बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [2]।
- बुखार उतारने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें — तेज़ तापमान संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है [2]।
- 16 साल से छोटे बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।
- 3 महीने से छोटे, 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले, चिकनपॉक्स या निर्जलीकरण वाले बच्चे को इबुप्रोफेन न दें [2]।
- दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर है — अपने डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार दें।

डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ अगर: बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो [1]; साँस लेने में तकलीफ हो [1]; मुँह से कुछ भी न ले पाए [1]; 2 महीने से छोटा या कम प्रतिरक्षा वाला हो [1]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Bukhar 102°F (38.9°C) hone par paracetamol de sakte hain, aur yeh bukhar aur bechaini mein aaram deta hai [1][4]. AEPap ke mutabik, paracetamol har 4-6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, aur din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Isse zyada dene se liver ko nuksan ho sakta hai [3].

Dose bachche ke wazan ke hisaab se tay hoti hai, umar se nahi [3]. PediBot ka dose calculator sirf paracetamol aur ibuprofen ke liye hai, isliye wazan daal kar sahi dose nikaal lein [3]. Dawa packet ya leaflet par likhi dose bhi zaroor padhein [5].

Agar bachche ko aaram na mile ya takleef ho, to doctor se milein — doctor ka intezaar karne ki zaroorat nahi [3]. Agar aapne packet par likhe se zyada paracetamol de diya hai, to turant medical advice lein [7].

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi hona asthma ya bronquiolitis jaisi saans ki takleef ka ek lakshan ho sakta hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ke symptoms mein raat ko ya subah jaldi khansi, saans phoolna aur seeti jaisi awaaz shaamil hain [1]. SEUP ke mutabik bronquiolitis mein bhi khansi ho sakti hai, khaas taur par raat ko [3].

Ghar par aaram karein, khoob saari tarshaan (liquid) dein, saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer istemaal karein, aur saline nasal drops ya spray dein [6]. Khansi ke syrup khud na dein — SEUP ke mutabik yeh faydemand nahi hain [2]. Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor se poochein [6].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans tez ya mushkil ho rahi ho [7]
- Honton ka rang neela-purple ho jaye [7]
- Doodh peena band kar de ya vomit kare [7]
- Paani kam ho — paani kam aana, muh sookha [7]
- Bahut sust ya rone wala ho [7]

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Mere bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli — sabse pehle yeh jaan lena zaroori hai ki yeh kaun sa rash ho sakta hai.

Agar dane chhote, ubhre hue hain aur khujli ya chubhan ke saath hain, to yeh heat rash (prickly heat) ho sakta hai. Yeh takleef deta hai lekin aam taur par harmless hota hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6].

Ghar par kya karein:
- Skin ko thanda rakhein — dheele cotton kapde pehnayein, halki bedding use karein, thande paani se nahayein [6].
- Khujli ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya ice pack, towel mein lipta hua) 20 minute tak lagayein [6].
- Dane ko kuraidein nahi, thapthapayein ya sehlayein [6].
- Khushbu wale shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Munh ke aas-paas sujan ho ya saans lene mein dikkat ho [5].

Agar dane chhote safed ya peele hain (milia), to yeh aam taur par kuch hafton mein khud chale jate hain aur ilaaj ki zaroorat nahi hoti [1].

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
text:
Aapke bachche ko sir ka chot laga hai aur ek baar ulti hui hai. SEUP ke mutabik sir ki chot ke baad ulti, sar dard, chakkar aana aur neend aana aam lakshan hain [1]. Ghar par pehle 24 ghante bachche par nazar rakhein [5].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Ulti baar-baar ho rahi ho [2][4]
- Sar dard badhta jaaye ya theek na ho [2][4]
- Confusion, behoshi ya jagane par na jaage [2][4]
- Chalne, bolne ya santulan mein dikkat [2][4]
- Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aaye [4]

Agar bachcha 1 saal se chhota hai aur sir par sujan ya bada cut hai, to turant dikhayein [3].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Bacche ka kabz aur potty ke waqt rona aam baat hai, lekin ise dekha jaana chahiye. NHS ke mutabik kabz un kai kaaranon mein se ek hai jinki wajah se bacche rote hain [3].

Kya karein: bacche ko aaram se pakdein aur tasalli dein; kabhi-kabhi iske alawa zyada kuch nahi kiya ja sakta [1]. Agar doodh pilate waqt rona ho, to breastfeeding mein positioning aur attachment sudhaarne se madad mil sakti hai [5]. Kabz ke liye bacche ko paani ya juice dene ki salah apne doctor se lein.

Doctor se milein agar:
- rona rukta hi nahi aur tasalli se bhi shaant na ho [7]
- rona unke normal rone jaisa na lage [7]
- bukhaar ho ya doodh peena band kar de [7]
- 8 ghante se peshaab na aaya ho [7]
- peshaab ya potty mein khoon dikhe

Turant madad lein agar bacche ko daura aaye, saans lene mein dikkat ho, ya skin neeli/pale ho [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, jaise bronchiolitis ya RSV, jo shuruaat mein zukam jaisa lagta hai aur kuch dinon mein badh sakta hai [2][5]. Aise waqt par bachche ko shaant rakhein, seedha baithayein, aur thoda-thoda doodh ya paani pilate rahein taaki wo hydrated rahe [5].

Madad turant lein agar:
- Saans lene mein dikkat, pet andar khinch raha ho ya tez saans [5]
- Saans lene mein rukawat ho [5]
- Hoth, jeebh ya skin neeli ya grey ho jaye [5]
- Bachcha sust ho aur uth na paaye [5]
- Doodh peena ya khana kaafi kam ho gaya ho [5]

Agar bachcha 3 mahine se chhota hai aur use bukhar hai, ya 3 mahine se bada hai aur bukhar 39°C ya zyada hai, to bhi doctor se milein [5].

q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
Meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi — WHO ke mutabik sust hona aur jag nahi pana bachchon mein sepsis ke signs ho sakte hain, aur sepsis ek medical emergency hai [2]. Aise bachche ko turant medical care leni chahiye [2].

Raste mein ya care ka intezaar karte waqt, bachche ko karwat par lita dein aur munh mein kuch na daalein [3]. Bachche ko kuch khilane-pilane ki koshish karein, lekin agar wo pee nahi pa raha ya bahut kam pee raha hai to us par zor na dein [5].

WHO ke mutabik bachchon mein sepsis ke signs ye hain [2]:
- Tez saans lena
- Jhatke aana (convulsions)
- Chehra peela padna
- Sust hona ya jag nahi pana
- Chhoote par thanda lagna

Paanch saal se chhote bachchon mein khana-peena mushkil hona, baar-baar ulti ya peshaab na aana bhi ho sakta hai [2].

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
Mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai — tez saans lena (taquipnea) chhote bachchon mein pneumonia ka ek nishaan hai, khaansi ho ya na ho, bukhaar ho ya na ho [6]. RSV ya bronchiolitis mein bhi saans tez ho sakti hai aur khaansi ke saath wheezing ya saans lene mein dikkat badh sakti hai [2][3].

Abhi kya karein: bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, kapde dheele karein, aur thoda-thoda karke baar-baar doodh ya paani pilate rahein — bronchiolitis mein bachcha kam khaata-peeta hai aur dehydration ka khatra hota hai [3]. Saans lene mein madad ke liye koi dawa khud na dein; dawa ke baare mein doctor hi batayega.

Yeh cheezein turant batayein (aapke doctor ya emergency department ko):
- Seene ki pasliyan andar kheench rahi hain ya pet andar dhas raha hai [3][6]
- Naak se grunting ki awaaz, ya saans lene mein rukawat [3]
- Hont, jeebh ya skin neeli ya grey ho rahi hai [3]
- Bachcha bahut sust ho gaya hai, uth nahi raha [3]
- Doodh/paani bilkul chhod diya, ya 12 ghante se peshaab nahi [3]

Agar aapko lage ki bachcha theek nahi lag raha, to apni samajh par bharosa karein [3].

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A bad night-time cough in a 2-year-old is often whooping cough, which causes coughing bouts that are worse at night and can last for several weeks [2]. Croup is another cause: a barking, seal-like cough that is also often worse at night [5].

Keep the room cool and give small sips of fluid often. If your child seems to be struggling, get help rather than waiting.

Get medical help if:
- The cough is very bad and getting worse [4]
- Lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [4]
- Breathing looks hard or shallow [4]
- Chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing [4]
- Seizures (fits) [4]

If your child is under 6 months old and has these symptoms, get help urgently [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by more than one illness, and measles is one of them: it causes a red, blotchy rash that usually starts on the head and works its way down the body, along with fever, cough, a runny nose and red, watery eyes [2][4]. The rash usually appears 3 to 5 days after those first symptoms and lasts 4 to 8 days before fading on its own [4].

Measles has no specific treatment, but the MMR vaccine prevents it [2]. Keep your child comfortable and watch them closely.

Get help if your child has:
- Trouble breathing or fast breathing [4]
- A stiff neck, confusion, or a seizure [4]
- Severe diarrhoea or signs of dehydration [4]
- An ear infection (ear pain, pulling at the ear) [4]
- Eyes that are very red and painful, or vision changes [4]

Complications are more common in children under five, so a child this age should be seen by your doctor [4].

[4] WHO — "Sarampión", section "Signos y síntomas", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/es/news-roo

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling or wheezing noise with a congested chest in a 6-month-old is often caused by a viral infection of the small airways, which is common in babies under 2 years old [4]. Most cases are mild and can be managed at home with their doctor's follow-up [5].

Keep feeding them as normally as possible, in smaller amounts more often if they tire easily, and let them sleep propped up rather than flat [5]. There is no medicine that cures this infection; it usually improves over about 2 weeks, though the cough can last longer [5].

While you get help, watch for:
- Faster breathing or ribs pulling in [6]
- Trouble finishing feeds [5]
- Changes in colour or general condition [5]
- Fever [5]

In babies under 3 months, or those born early or with other health problems, breathing difficulty can become more serious [5].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में उतर जाता है, और ज़्यादातर बच्चों की देखभाल घर पर ही की जा सकती है [1][3]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें; भूख लगे तो खाना दें; रात में भी नियमित रूप से जाँचते रहें; और बच्चे को घर पर ही रखें [3]। बेचैनी या तकलीफ़ हो तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफ़ेन दी जा सकती है — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए ठीक है [3]। 5 किलो वज़न और 6 महीने की उम्र में आइबुप्रोफ़ेन देने से पहले डॉक्टर से पूछें [2]। खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है [3]।

डॉक्टर से मदद लें अगर:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा [2]
- बुखार के साथ दाने भी हों [2]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [2]
- खाना न चाहे, या हमेशा जैसा न लगे और आपको चिंता हो [2]
- पेशाब कम आना, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना [2]

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाएँ या स्पंज न करें — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ़ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य बताता है [3]। बुखार आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- 3 महीने से कम उम्र और 38C या ज़्यादा बुखार [7]
- बुखार के साथ दाने [7]
- 5 दिन या ज़्यादा बुखार [7]
- खाने से मना करे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे [7]
- पेशाब कम आना, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना [7]

6 महीने के बच्चे को 5 किलो वज़न होने पर इबुप्रोफेन न दें [7]। पैरासिटामोल की खुराक बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर है [7]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी जैसी आवाज़ होना सांस की नली में रुकावट के कारण हो सकता है, जिसे घरघराहट कहते हैं — यह अक्सर सांस की वायरल बीमारियों से होता है, और ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं से सुधरता है [2]। ऐसे लक्षण अस्थमा में भी दिखते हैं, जिसमें सांस की नलियां सूजकर सिकुड़ जाती हैं और सीटी की आवाज़, खांसी और छाती में जकड़न होती है [4]।

अभी बच्चे को सीधा बैठाएं और शांत रखें, और उसे लेकर डॉक्टर के पास जाएं — अस्थमा के लक्षण दिखने पर स्वास्थ्य कर्मी से मिलना चाहिए [5]। रास्ते में बच्चे को आराम से बैठी हालत में रखें और उसे खाने-पीने के लिए मजबूर न करें।

इन पर तुरंत मदद लें:
- तेज़ खांसी और सांस लेने में गंभीर तकलीफ [7]
- चेहरे, होंठ या नाखूनों का पीला या नीला पड़ना [7]
- सांस लेते समय तेज़, कर्कश आवाज़ [3]
- बच्चे का बेहतर न होना या बिगड़ना [3]

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे दाने छोटे कीड़ों (स्केबीज़) से हो सकते हैं, जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं और तेज़ खुजली करते हैं; ये अक्सर उंगलियों के बीच शुरू होते हैं और आमतौर पर घर पर ही इलाज हो जाता है [4]। स्केबीज़ त्वचा से त्वचा के संपर्क से फैलता है, और यह सफ़ाई की कमी से नहीं होता [1]।

अभी: त्वचा को ठंडा रखें — ढीले सूती कपड़े पहनाएँ, हल्का बिस्तर, ठंडा स्नान, और पानी खूब पिलाएँ। खुजली शांत करने के लिए ठंडी चीज़ (गीला कपड़ा या तौलिये में लपेटी आइस पैक) 20 मिनट तक लगाएँ, और खुजाने की जगह थपथपाएँ। सुगंधित साबुन या क्रीम न लगाएँ [6]। नाखून काटें ताकि खुजाने से त्वचा में संक्रमण न हो [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगे या एक्ज़िमा जैसी दूसरी त्वचा समस्या हो [1]
- कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों [1]
- फार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा करने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]
- घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो [1]

इलाज के बाद खुजली कुछ हफ़्ते तक रह सकती है [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के हल्के दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, लेकिन ये सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो सकता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]।

टीके समय पर लगवाना ज़रूरी है ताकि सबसे अच्छी सुरक्षा मिले; अगर कोई टीका छूट गया हो तो अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]। एमएमआर (यहाँ MMRV के रूप में) आमतौर पर एक साल की उम्र में पहली खुराक दी जाती है [1] — भारत में उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती हैं, इसलिए अपने डॉक्टर से पुष्टि कर लें।

अगर टीके के बाद कोई गंभीर लक्षण दिखे, तो अपने डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi 3 saal ke bachche mein aam hai — kai haalaton mein iska matlab hai asthma, jo bachchon mein khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. Laringitis mein bhi bachche raat bhar kaafi khaanste hain aur theek se sote nahi [6].

Ghar par: agar bukhar ho to liquids do aur aam bukhar ki dawa de sakte hain [6]. Kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vapouriser istemaal karo, aur saline nasal drops ya spray se naak saaf rakho [4]. Khaansi ya zukaam ki koi dawa dene se pehle apne doctor se poochho — bachchon ke liye kuch ingredients theek nahi hote [4].

Doctor se turant milo agar:
- Saans lene mein dikkat ya tez saans [4]
- Honton ya chehre par neela rang [5]
- Bahut bechaini ya neend mein na aana [7]
- Seene ka dhadakna, pasliyan dikhna [7]
- Bukhar 4 din se zyada [4]

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko bed se girne ke baad sar par chot lagi hai. SEUP ke mutabiq sar par chot ke aam lakshan hain: sar dard, bhram, ulti, neend aana aur sust ho jana [1].

Ghar par kya karein: baby ko 24 se 48 ghante aaram karayein, koi jismani khel ya screen nahi [2]. Khana-peena uski bhookh ke hisaab se jaari rakhein [6]. Agar sar dard ho to dawa ki matra doctor batayega [6]. Zyada gehri chot mein har 4 ghante baby ko jaga kar dekhein [6].

Turant doctor ke paas jaayein agar:
- Tez ya badhta sar dard, ya dawa se bhi na kam ho [2]
- Baar baar ulti [2]
- Bechaini ya jagaana mushkil ho [2]
- Vyavhaar mein badlav, bolne ya chalne mein dikkat [2]
- Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aaye [2]

Chot ke pehle 24 ghante baby par nazar rakhein [3].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche par red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur inme se kuch aam hain. WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) me tez khujli hoti hai, khaas taur par raat me, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lakeerein dikhti hain [2]. Chhote bachchon me yeh rash zyada gambhir ho sakta hai, khaas taur par hatheliyon, pairon ke talwon aur sar ki twacha par [2].

Ghar par kya karein: agar khujli hai to bachche ke naakhun chhote rakhein taaki khujaane se twacha na kate. Sarna doosron me aasani se failta hai, isliye jis bachche ko yeh ho, uske kapde aur bistar alag rakhein. Ilaaj cream ya dawa se hota hai, jo doctor likhta hai [5].

Doctor se kab milein:
- Tez khujli jo raat me badh jaaye [2]
- Ungliyon, kalaiyon ya kamar par dane aur lakeerein [2]
- Twacha par ghale ya infection ke nishaan [5]
- Saans lene me dikkat, hoth ya chehra sujna, ya bachcha sust ya behosh lage [7]

Yeh jaankari WHO aur NHS par aadharit hai.

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text: Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai: polio se bachne ka sabse asardar tareeka tikakaran hai, aur bachchon ko polio ke khilaf pura primary tikakaran lena chahiye [6]. Spain ke national schedule mein polio (VPI) wali vaccine 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein di jaati hai, aur 6 saal par booster diya jaata hai [3]. Jo bachche 2, 4, 6 aur 18 mahine par 4 doses le chuke hain, unhe 6 saal par polio ke bina wali dTpa dose milti hai [3]. Apne bachche ke liye sahi umar aur doses ke baare mein apne doctor se poochhein, kyunki har desh ka schedule alag ho sakta hai.

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea is usually a sign of an infection in the digestive tract, and it can be caused by many different bacteria, viruses and parasites, according to the WHO [6]. It is treated with oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1][4]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Give ORS in small amounts, and keep breastfeeding [1][3]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [3].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so watery and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

Consult a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1].

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये सामान्य दुष्प्रभाव हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के 6-7 दिनों बाद भी हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं, जो अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

टीके के एक-दो घंटे बाद बच्चे को पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है; खुराक के बारे में टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]। बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न के हिसाब से खुराक तय होती है, इसलिए अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बुखार 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हो [5]
- इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए [5]

टीकाकरण की उम्र भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness happens when the body can't cool itself, usually after too long in the heat or sun [3]. Dizziness is one of the signs to take seriously: if your child is dizzy, get medical help right away, according to MedlinePlus [3].

While you wait, move them to a cool, shady place, take off extra clothing, put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to bring the temperature down [6]. Do not give fever medicine for heat illness — use physical cooling measures instead [5].

Get urgent help if:
- Fever above 39°C that doesn't come down with home measures [7]
- Loss of consciousness or seizures [7]
- Confusion, trouble speaking or moving [7]
- Persistent vomiting, can't keep fluids down [7]

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text:
Baby ko thehri khaana (solids) takreeban 6 mahine ki umar se shuru karein [2]. Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke kitna kha raha hai — ahem yeh hai ke woh khaane ki aadat ho jaye; zyada tar energy aur nutrients abhi bhi doodh (breast milk ya first infant formula) se milte hain [2].

6 mahine tak sirf doodh dena behtar hai: is se bachay ko bimari aur infection se hifazat milti hai, aur itne waqt mein woh nigalne aur chabane ke liye tayyar ho jata hai [4]. Doodh ke saath saath mukhtalif qism ke khaane dena achi aadat banata hai; aahista aahista miqdar aur variety barhayein [2].

Agar bacha waqt se pehle paida hua ho, to solids kab shuru karein is par apne doctor se mashwara karein [2].

Yeh bhi khayal rakhein:
- 5 saal se chhote bachon ko sabut nuts na dein — choke ho sakte hain; weaning shuru hone se nuts pise ya ground kar ke de sakte hain [5].
- Nut butter toast par laga kar dein, akela na dein [5].
- Agar khandaan mein allergy ki history ho, to koi bhi nut dene se pehle doctor se poochein [5].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Loose, watery stools like these are usually gastroenteritis, an infection of the gut that causes more frequent, softer stools, sometimes with tummy pain, vomiting and fever [3]. It is usually not serious, but the main risk is dehydration [2].

What to do now: give an oral rehydration solution — a precise mix of water, sugar and salts — in small amounts often, and offer the amount you were told after each loose stool or vomit [3]. Keep breastfeeding normally, even more often if your child wants it, and keep offering a near-normal diet in smaller, more frequent portions; avoid fatty foods, sweets, juices and sports drinks [7]. Do not give diarrhoea or vomiting medicines without asking your doctor [1].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine or sunken eyes [1]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [1]
- Refusing to eat or drink [1]
- Persistent or severe tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [1]
- Vomiting a lot, or green or bloody vomit [7]

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe, and it works well: protection starts within 2 weeks of the vaccine, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps, according to the NHS [2]. If someone does get mumps after being vaccinated, the symptoms are usually much milder [2].

In India, the ages and doses for MMR follow India's national immunisation schedule, so check your daughter's schedule with your doctor or health worker for when her doses are due.

For children born prematurely or with other risk factors, the MMR can be given earlier — at 6 to 11 months — if there is a risk of exposure, especially to measles, though that dose does not count as the first scheduled dose, according to the AEP [1]. Living with someone who has a weakened immune system is not a reason to skip the vaccine [4].

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text:
Yes, you can give banana. Soft fruits such as banana are listed as good finger foods once your baby has started solids, according to the NHS [5].

At 6 months, how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating — they still get most energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [3]. Offer finger foods at each meal: pieces about the size of your own finger, long enough to grip with a bit sticking out [5]. Banana works well as slices of soft fruit [5]. Always sit your baby upright in a high chair with a safety harness, and never leave them unattended [4]. Offer sips of water from an open or free-flow cup with meals [4].

Avoid hard foods like whole nuts or raw carrot and apple, to reduce choking risk [5]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your doctor for advice on when to start solids [3].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach pain and constipation often go together, and most abdominal pain in children is harmless and gets better on its own — constipation is one of the usual causes, according to the SEUP [2].

To help the constipation: offer more fluids, preferably water, and more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Don't replace fruit with juice, as juice has little fibre [3]. Keep to a regular routine and don't let your child hold in the urge to go to the toilet [3]. Don't give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3].

See your doctor if:
- Bad stomach pain, or your child is very down and complaining a lot [3]
- Blood in the poo [3]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down food or drink [3]
- Pain that is intense and continuous, or your child seems generally unwell [4]

Most cases of childhood constipation are not caused by any disease [3].

q: मेरी बेटी को तीन बार उल्टी हुई है, क्या ओआरएस दे सकती हूं?
text:
तीन बार उल्टी होने पर ओआरएस दिया जा सकता है — दस्त और उल्टी का इलाज ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ओआरएस) से किया जाता है, जो साफ़ पानी, नमक और चीनी का मिश्रण है, और यह शरीर में खोए पानी और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स की भरपाई करता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्ची को थोड़े-थोड़े घूँट में बार-बार तरल दें, क्योंकि उल्टी होने पर छोटे घूँट लेना बेहतर रहता है [6]। अगर वह स्तनपान या बोतल से दूध पीती है तो दूध जारी रखें — उल्टी हो रही हो तो थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में ज़्यादा बार दें [6]। ठोस आहार लेने वाले बच्चों को दूध के बीच-बीच में थोड़ा पानी दें [6]। दस्त के दौरान पौष्टिक भोजन जारी रखें [1]।

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text:
It is not possible to say from these sources that the bumps are hives. Small itchy bumps can have different causes, and the sources describe several: eczema causes dry, itchy skin with a rash in the creases of the elbows and behind the knees, and scratching can make it redder and itchier [3]; scabies causes intense itching, often worse at night, with bumps and lines on the fingers, wrists, arms, legs and around the waist [4]; measles causes a red spotted rash that usually starts on the head and spreads down the body, with fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes [6].

Because the cause is not clear from your message, the sources do not give one treatment to start at home. A pharmacist can advise on antihistamines for an itchy hives-type rash, but this may not be suitable for young children [7].

Get medical help if your child has any of these:
- Swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue [7]
- Fast or difficult breathing, or a tight throat [7]
- Skin, tongue or lips turning blue, grey or pale [7]
- Sudden confusion, drowsiness or dizziness, or fainting [7]
- Limp, floppy or not responding normally [7]

q: my daughter has fever after coming back from a trip
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, a high temperature is usually the body's natural response to fighting an infection, and it often settles within 1 to 4 days [1][7]. Fever is not an illness in itself — it is a sign the body is fighting a virus or bacteria [3]. Because your daughter was recently travelling, the NHS advises contacting your doctor when you return home if she was sick with a fever while away [6].

What to do now: offer plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration [3]. You can take her temperature with a digital thermometer under the arm [1]. Do not undress or sponge her down to cool her, and do not wrap her in too many clothes or blankets [7]. Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [7]. The dose of any fever medicine depends on her age and weight, so follow your doctor's or the leaflet's guidance.

Get medical care if:
- Fever lasts 5 days or more [7]
- She has a rash with the fever [7]
- She is not eating or not her usual self [7]
- She seems dehydrated — fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, no tears [7]
- Diarrhoea does not go away, or she becomes dehydrated [6]

How old is your child? With the age I can make this more precise.

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are introduced alongside it, according to the WHO [3]. Start with small amounts — just a few pieces or teaspoons — and increase gradually as your baby grows [1][3]. Offer food before the usual milk feed, when your baby is not too tired or too hungry, and let them set the pace [1]. Keep offering different foods even if rejected; it can take 10 tries or more before a new food is accepted [1]. Breast milk or first infant formula stays the main drink through the first year — do not give whole cows', goats' or sheep's milk as a main drink before 1 year [1]. From around 6 months, offer sips of water with meals from an open or free-flow cup [1]. Aim for 2–3 meals a day at 6–8 months [3].

q: my 4 year old has severe cough and catarrh
text:
A severe cough with catarrh (a runny nose) can be the first phase of whooping cough, which often starts like a cold with a runny nose, fever, red watery eyes and a mild cough, according to the Government of Canada [4]. In the second phase the cough becomes more severe, coming in fits that can make it hard to breathe and may end in vomiting [4].

Whooping cough is treated with antibiotics if it is diagnosed within 3 weeks of the cough starting; antibiotics may not reduce the symptoms but help stop it spreading [6]. Hospital treatment is usually needed for severe whooping cough [6].

Get medical help if:
- Your child has a very bad cough that is getting worse [7]
- Your child is finding it hard to breathe properly [7]
- Your child's lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [7]
- Your child has chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing [7]
- Your child has seizures (fits) [7]

q: my 5 year old fell down and hurt his leg leg is swollen
text:
A swollen leg after a fall is most likely a sprain or strain, and most of these can be treated at home, according to the NHS [3]. The injured area being swollen or bruised is a typical sign of a sprain or strain [3].

What to do now: rest the leg, keep it raised, and avoid letting him put weight on it while it is painful. If you give pain relief, the dose depends on his weight — paracetamol or ibuprofen can be used, and PediBot's dose calculator covers both.

Get help if:
- He cannot put weight on the leg or use it normally [3]
- The pain, tenderness or weakness is severe or getting worse [3]
- The swelling or bruising is extensive or increasing [3]
- You are worried about how the leg looks or he seems unwell

If he also hit his head, watch for vomiting, worsening headache, confusion, or difficulty speaking or walking, and seek care for those [4][6].

q: my 18 month old is refusing food and crying when chewing

q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text:
Watery stools with weakness in a 3-year-old is usually gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious but can lead to dehydration [3]. The main treatment is rehydration with oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the diarrhoea and reduce stool volume, according to the WHO [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace losses, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your doctor, according to the SEUP [2]. Offer food in smaller amounts more often, avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices, and avoid sports drinks [7].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [2]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [2]
- Refuses to eat or drink [2]
- Persistent or intense belly pain, or stools with a lot of blood [2]
- Vomiting a lot, or not keeping down solids or liquids [7]

q: what can I give my 2 year old for diarrhoea

For diarrhoea in a 2-year-old, the main treatment is oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, according to the WHO [1]. - Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

q: my baby is not passing urine as much as usual
text:
A baby who is not passing urine as much as usual may be dehydrated. In babies and young children, signs of dehydration include a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, and not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Babies and small children are more likely to become dehydrated because they are more prone to diarrhoea or vomiting [2].

Offer your baby fluids often. If they are still feeding, keep breastfeeding or giving formula; if they are on solids, offer small sips of water or an oral rehydration solution frequently.

- Confusion [5]
- Fainting [5]
- No urine at all [5]
- Fast heartbeat [5]
- Fast breathing [5]

Also see your doctor if your baby has a dry mouth and tongue, cries without tears, is unusually sleepy or irritable, has sunken eyes, or has a high fever [5].

Most head bumps in children are minor, and it is common for a child to seem well right after a fall [3]. The SEUP advises watching your child closely for the first 24 hours after the blow, looking for signs of seriousness [2].

q: my 6 month old has started eating food, what should I give first
text:
At around 6 months, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to the idea of eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [1]. Give a variety of foods alongside breast or formula milk, and increase the amount and variety gradually until they can eat the same foods as the rest of the family in smaller portions [1].

Start with iron-rich foods, and introduce the different foods one at a time, following your family's customs, to broaden the diet [4][6]. There is no evidence that delaying potentially allergenic foods beyond 6 months prevents allergy; introducing them early in small amounts may even reduce the chance of allergy later [4].

If your baby was born prematurely, ask your doctor for advice on when to start solid foods [1].

q: my 4 year old has high fever and shivering
text:
A high temperature is 38C or more, and it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. Shivering happens because the body is raising its temperature to fight the infection — it is part of the fever itself, not a sign that things are getting worse [6].

What to do now: keep them drinking enough fluids to prevent dehydration [2]. Do not undress them or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [3]. You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen if they are uncomfortable; the dose depends on the child's weight, and our dose calculator covers those two medicines [2][6]. Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [3].

Get help if your child:
- has a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it [3]
- has a stiff neck, is bothered by light, or has a fit for the first time [3]
- is drowsy and hard to wake, or is confused or extremely agitated [3]
- has difficulty breathing, or unusually cold hands and feet [3]
- has a fever lasting 5 days or more, or is not their usual self and you are worried [3]

q: my son has malaria medicine but still has fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, malaria is a serious infection that always requires treatment with medicine, and the right medicine depends on the type of malaria, whether the parasite is resistant, and the child's weight or age [3]. Fever that continues despite treatment is a reason to go back to the doctor: early diagnosis and treatment prevents deaths, and suspected malaria should be confirmed with a diagnostic test [3]. Do not give a medicine other than the one prescribed, and do not change the dose yourself — the doctor chooses the treatment based on the child's weight and age [3].

Get medical help now if your child has any of these:
- Confusion [1]
- Seizures [1]
- Difficulty breathing [1]
- Extreme tiredness [1]

Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1].

q: my child fell and hit his head but is playing normally
text:
Most head injuries are not serious, but any symptoms need medical help, according to the NHS [2]. Your child is playing normally, which is reassuring, but it is still worth watching him closely for the first 24 hours after the knock [3].

Let him rest — no sport, no screens — for 24 to 48 hours, then return to normal activities gradually [4]. He can eat and drink as usual, and he can sleep; after a bigger knock, it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. If he has a headache, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose your doctor indicates [6].

Get help if he has:
- been knocked out and cannot be woken [2]
- a fit or seizure [2]
- clear fluid or blood from the ears or nose [2][4]

q: my 4 year old has cough with phlegm at night
text:
A cough with phlegm at night is common with colds and other respiratory infections in young children [2]. There is no cure for a cold; it usually goes away on its own, and most people feel better after a week or two [2].

What helps while it passes: plenty of fluids, rest, and a clean humidifier or cool-mist vaporizer in the room [2]. Saline nose drops or sprays can also help [2]. Do not give aspirin to a child [2]. Cough and cold medicines often contain ingredients not recommended for young children, so talk to your child's doctor before giving any [2]. Some contain pain relievers, so check labels to avoid doubling up [2].

Talk to your doctor if your child has trouble breathing or is breathing fast, is dehydrated, has a fever lasting more than 4 days, symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement, or symptoms that improve then return or worsen [2]. The SEUP also lists as reasons to seek urgent care: poor general condition, drowsiness or extreme irritability, difficulty breathing (fast breathing, ribs showing, chest sinking), chest or side pain when breathing, poor colour, or persistently refusing food and fluids [5].

q: when to start feeding puree to 6 months old
text:
From around 6 months of age you can start solid foods, and you can begin with purées, mashed food or soft finger foods — there is no right or wrong way, according to the NHS [1][2].

If you start with purée, move on to mashed, lumpy or finger foods as soon as your baby can manage them; this helps them learn to chew and swallow [2]. Some babies prefer smooth food on a spoon at first and need a little longer with new textures — keep offering lumpy textures and they will get used to them [2].

Breast milk still matters now: between 6 and 12 months it can provide half or more of a child's energy needs, so keep breastfeeding alongside the new foods, according to the WHO [5].

q: is 6 in 1 vaccine safe for my baby
text:
The 6-in-1 vaccine is given as part of the routine baby schedule, and the ingredients in vaccines are used in very small amounts with no evidence they are harmful at those levels, according to the NHS [1]. Aluminium salts, one common ingredient, have been used safely in routine infant vaccines for more than 70 years, and no harmful effects have been seen with vaccines containing them [1].

Serious allergic reactions to any vaccine are rare and usually happen within minutes, when the person giving the vaccine is trained to treat them straight away [7].

If you are worried about your baby having a vaccine, or are not sure whether they can have it, speak to your doctor or nurse [7]. In the Philippines, the ages and doses for the 6-in-1 follow the national schedule, so check the timing with your baby's doctor.

q: my daughter has small red spots after fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, small red spots appearing after a fever fit a pattern doctors recognise. In roseola (exantema súbito), a high fever lasts 3 to 4 days with no other symptoms, then the fever drops and a faint, flat, widespread rash appears and lasts about 48 hours, according to PUC Chile [4]. It is diagnosed by this sequence of events, and there is no vaccine to prevent it [4]. Febrile seizures are a known complication [4].

Measles is another cause: it starts with cold-like symptoms — high temperature, runny nose, sneezing, cough, red watery eyes — followed by a rash a few days later, and small white spots may appear inside the mouth, according to the NHS [3]. In measles the rash usually starts on the face at the hairline and spreads down the body, and the fever may spike above 104°F when the rash appears [1].

Because the two look different in how they start, have your child seen by a doctor to sort out which one this is.

q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby
text: At around 6 months, start with a variety of foods alongside breast milk or first infant formula — how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating [3]. q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol
text:
102 °F = 38.9 °C.

Yes — paracetamol (Calpol) can help if your child is distressed or uncomfortable because of a high temperature, according to the NHS [3]. It comes as a painkiller for children that relieves pain and high temperature [4].

The main goal is your child's comfort, not bringing the fever itself down [2]. Make sure they drink plenty of liquids and are not over-wrapped, and do not force them to eat if they have no appetite [2]. Paracetamol and ibuprofen both work, and are given at the dose your paediatrician recommends, every 6 to 8 hours [2]. Do not alternate them routinely every 3 to 4 hours [2]. Do not bathe your child in cold water or use wet cloths — it is unpleasant and does not work [2].

Get help if your child is:
- listless, barely responsive or very irritable [7]
- having trouble breathing [7]
- has skin spots that do not fade when pressed [7]
- cannot keep down solids or liquids [7]

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text:
Yes — oral rehydration salts (ORS) are one of the main treatments for diarrhoea, according to the WHO [1]. ORS is a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Give it in small amounts often, and keep offering nutrient-rich foods and breast milk during the episode [1]. Zinc supplements are also part of treatment: they shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses [3].

See a health professional if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine or sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so watery and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

q: le ha salido un sarpullido rojo por las piernas y le pica
text:
Un sarpullido rojo que pica en las piernas puede ser una urticaria: ronchas o placas rojas y elevadas que pican mucho, y que van apareciendo en una zona mientras desaparecen de otra [3]. En la infancia, la mayoría de las urticarias las causa una infección, y la causa alérgica es menos frecuente [3].

También puede tratarse de una reacción a picaduras de insectos, que da lesiones que pican intensamente y aparecen sobre todo en brazos y piernas [6]. Conviene evitar que se rasque, porque el rascado puede infectar las lesiones [6].

Consulta a tu doctor si:
- Le cuesta respirar o tragar [3].
- Se le hinchan las manos, los pies, los codos o la cara [3].
- Las lesiones se infectan o supuran por el rascado [6].
- El sarpullido no mejora o se extiende [6].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre y rigidez en el cuello
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Rigidez de nuca: hay que descartar una meningitis ahora mismo
text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

La meningitis es la inflamación del tejido que rodea el cerebro y la médula espinal, y puede agravarse muy rápido, según MedlinePlus [7]. La fiebre con rigidez en el cuello es uno de los signos por los que hay que buscar atención médica de inmediato [7].

Mientras llega la ayuda: mantén al niño acompañado, sin sobreabrigarlo y en un lugar ventilado, y ofrécele líquidos a sorbos si puede tragar [5]. No lo bañes en agua fría ni le pongas paños húmedos, porque resulta desagradable y no sirve [5]. No le des nada por la boca si está somnoliento o no responde con claridad.

Otros signos que acompañan a la meningitis y conviene vigilar: dolor de cabeza fuerte, náuseas o vómitos [7]; y puntos rojos en la piel que no desaparecen al apretarlos [4].

q: mi hija se ha caido de un segundo piso pero parece estar bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Caída por las escaleras o de más de un metro, o llanto que no se calma tras un golpe: que lo vea un médico hoy
text:
Un golpe en la cabeza puede causar dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria pasajera, mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia, según la SEUP [1]. Las lesiones en la cabeza pueden ser leves o graves, y las cerradas no siempre son menos graves que las abiertas [4].

Mientras la ven, mantén a tu hija en reposo físico y mental, sin deportes ni pantallas, y que la reincorporación a sus actividades sea gradual [6]. No le des nada de comer ni beber por si la tienen que valorar.

Señales para vigilar de camino al médico:
- Dolor de cabeza intenso o que no mejora [6]
- Vómitos repetidos [6]
- Desorientación o confusión, o muy irritable o difícil de despertar [6]
- Cambios de comportamiento, dificultad para hablar o caminar [6]
- Sangre o líquido claro por la nariz o los oídos [6]

Si tiene menos de tres meses, también hay que consultar [3].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre despues de vacunarse ayer

Si tu hijo tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre tras la vacuna necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre después de vacunarse es una reacción esperada y pasajera. El calendario de vacunación que se sigue en España lo marca el Ministerio de Sanidad, con las edades de cada vacuna según el calendario nacional [2].

Lo que puedes hacer ahora:
- Ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia y en pequeñas cantidades.

- Si tiene fiebre y malestar, puedes darle paracetamol o ibuprofeno; la dosis depende de su edad y su peso, así que consúltala con tu pediatra o en el prospecto [2].

Consulta a tu médico si:
- La fiebre es alta o no baja con las medidas habituales [2].
- El niño está decaído, irritable o no responde como siempre [2].
- Aparecen manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionar [2].
- La fiebre dura más de lo esperado o aparecen otros síntomas [2].

Si el niño es prematuro o tiene alguna condición de riesgo, coméntalo con su pediatra antes de dar por normal la reacción [1].

q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text:
La erupción de los dientes de leche empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, con los incisivos centrales inferiores, según el Manual de Pediatría de la PUC de Chile [6]. Que a los 9 meses todavía no le haya salido ninguno puede entrar dentro de la variación normal de cada bebé; la secuencia y el momento exacto varían de un niño a otro [6].

Mientras tanto, puedes revisarle la boca con calma: mira las encías por si están inflamadas o con heridas, y los rebordes donde saldrán los dientes [6]. Aprovecha para cuidar su higiene bucal desde ahora, porque la caries puede empezar temprano en los dientes que aún no se ven [6].

Consulta a tu pediatra o a un odontopediatra si a los 12-13 meses sigue sin aparecer ningún diente, o antes si notas las encías muy inflamadas, con sangrado o heridas [6].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text:
El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no se debe a un problema del corazón [1]. Cuando aparece después de hacer ejercicio, puede tratarse de una distensión o tirón muscular: suele empeorar al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo [1]. También puede ser ansiedad, que a veces cursa con presión o dolor en el pecho [3].

Lo que conviene hacer ahora es que descanse y evite el esfuerzo hasta que lo valore un médico [1]. No intentes diagnosticarlo por tu cuenta: si te preocupa, consulta a tu médico [1].

Busca ayuda médica urgente si el dolor:
- No desaparece o es como una opresión en el pecho [7].
- Se extiende al brazo, cuello, mandíbula, estómago o espalda [7].
- Se acompaña de sudor, náuseas, mareo o falta de aire [7].

Consulta también a tu médico si el dolor va y viene, o si desaparece rápido pero sigues preocupado [7].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Desmayo haciendo ejercicio, o con palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho: que lo vean en urgencias hoy
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, y en general ocurre cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. Después de un rato de reposo, los niños suelen recuperarse rápido, en un par de minutos [5].

Mientras se recupera, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado para que respire mejor [5]. Cuando el malestar y la debilidad hayan desaparecido, puede incorporarse despacio: primero sentada y, tras unos minutos, de pie [5]. Conviene que beba más líquidos, sobre todo cuando hace ejercicio [4].

Señales para consultar en urgencias:
- Tarda más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento [3].
- El desmayo ocurrió haciendo ejercicio o esfuerzo [3].
- Hubo palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho [3].
- Hubo sacudidas de brazos o piernas [3].
- Se orinó sin querer al final del episodio [3].
